executive_summary.executive_brief: The sole signal change today is a RE-FIRE on t2_hyperscaler_capex_revenue [→§3]: the computed 2-quarter rolling mean capex/OCF across MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN stands at 80.1% — well above the 50% full-fire threshold — with Amazon's 2-quarter rolling mean at 121.2% triggering the single-company strain overlay; per v3.39.7.3 Rule C the computed verdict is authoritative and overrides yesterday's Layer 2 'Reversed' call (which incorrectly used capex/revenue rather than capex/OCF as the denominator), restoring T2 fired count to 6/7 and applying Rule A probability adjustments [→§4]. The dominant macro story remains the Samsung strike cluster, now fully resolved: the planned 48,000-worker walkout was called off via an 11th-hour wage deal (Bloomberg 02:07 UTC, confirmed by 15+ subsequent sources through France 24 at 11:29 UTC), with Samsung distributing up to $26.6B in AI-driven bonuses averaging ~$338,000 per chip employee — the operative state is strike averted, production continuity confirmed, and the near-term HBM/DRAM supply tightening risk previously priced in is removed; separately, the Samsung 10-year bonus lock-in structure (Chosunbiz) introduces a modest near-term capex flexibility constraint that is directional confirmation of t2_capex_parabolic cost pressures at the supplier level [→§5]. On the big-mover front, SK Hynix surged +11.17% [→§1] — the largest single-session move in the coverage universe — while Samsung +8.51% both dramatically outperformed NVIDIA -1.75%, AMAT -0.96%, and Cerebras -2.23%, with memory pure-plays leading the semi tape in a sharp reversal of last week's relative weakness; the SK Hynix 5-day vs SOX spread is now +0.63pp, fully extinguishing the t3_relative_strength fire risk that was building last week [→§3]. The value-chain inference is direct: NVIDIA's Q1 FY27 print of $81.6B revenue with "demand gone parabolic" commentary and analyst estimates of $1T in hyperscaler capex by 2027 [→§5] → SK Hynix Cheongju mask fab reallocation toward HBM yield (DigiTimes) → DDR5/LPDDR5X wafer allocation tightens → Mirae Asset's LPDDR5X +81% QoQ and LPDDR4X +72% QoQ Q2 2026 contract price acceleration (primary source, published today) → t3_contract_decline remains firmly Not fired with the strongest anti-trigger evidence to date [→§4]. The macro backdrop is unambiguously bullish in the near term with CXMT's Shanghai Stock Exchange IPO review next week accelerating the medium-term China DRAM supply narrative — the most credible path to cycle turn in H2 2026–H1 2027 — while Micron's commentary that AI memory supply constraints will deepen through 2028 and Nomura's SK Hynix target of KRW 4,000,000 (implying 10.5x forward P/E vs current 5.07x) signal that sell-side consensus remains in full bull mode with zero downward EPS revisions in the 30-day window [→§4].
